Tier B with caveats: all five pooled sleep trials ran in India; in the two KSM-66 trials I checked (Langade 2019, Salve 2019) the extract was supplied by its maker (Ixoreal) with no funding statement, the other two KSM-66 trials (Kelgane 2020, Langade 2021) were not checked, and the Shoden trial was sponsored by its maker (Arjuna). No trial declared brand funding outright, so it is not N, but independent replication outside India is missing. Cheah 2021 rated the overall sleep evidence moderate certainty. Sensoril has no trial in the sleep meta-analysis. dose_min 250 mg applies to KSM-66 (Salve 2019); Shoden worked at 120 mg, so the floor depends on the extract; plain root powder was not studied. V3's 6 to 8 week framing was roughly right; its liver and thyroid flags are confirmed. Safety sources: LiverTox (captcha) and NIH ODS (HTTP 403) could not be opened, so the liver rows rest on Bjornsson 2020 and Philips 2023, the thyroid row on Sharma 2018, and the pregnancy row on standard label warnings. Regulatory context, not cited as evidence: Denmark banned it in supplements in 2023 and the Dutch RIVM advised against it in 2024 (NutraIngredients timeline, July 2026). Cost is an estimate.

safety.note: Safety while breastfeeding is not established, so a clinician's view comes first.
Rare liver injury has been reported, and it was most serious in people with existing liver disease.
In a small trial it shifted thyroid hormone levels, so thyroid medicine calls for a clinician check first.
Product labels warn against use during pregnancy.

items.name: Mouth tape
items.evidenceFor: better sleep in people without sleep apnea
items.evidenceSummary: A 2025 review found ten small, low-quality studies, mostly in people with sleep apnea or mouth breathing; a few saw less snoring. None tested people who sleep normally, and taping is risky with a blocked nose.
items.humanQuestion: Do you snore, or is it more about dry mouth?
items.notesInternal: V3 graded C off one small uncontrolled study in mild apnea (Lee 2022: 20 people, no control group). Rhee 2025 (systematic review) found ten poor-quality studies, none testing normal sleepers, and concluded the data do not support taping. Graded D for better sleep in people without sleep apnea (mechanism and anecdote only); the snoring signal in mild apnea is C at best. The main risks (blocked nose, moderate or severe apnea, regurgitation while taped) have no matching condition in the brief's safety list. Suggest adding a 'sleep-apnea-or-blocked-nose' condition with never-suggest, and a gate that routes loud snoring, gasping or witnessed breathing pauses to a clinician. Cost is an estimate (branded strips cost more, plain surgical tape far less).

safety.note: No studies include children, and taping carries breathing risks.

items.name: Eight Sleep / cooling mattress pad
items.evidenceFor: a little more deep sleep
items.evidenceSummary: The only studies of the product itself come from the company. In one blinded trial, a cooler mattress added about 7 minutes of deep sleep and a slightly slower heart rate. Heat disturbs sleep, so hot sleepers may gain most.
items.humanQuestion: Do you sleep hot, and is the cooling still on?
items.fitsInstead: A fan, lighter bedding and a cooler room, for far less.
items.notesInternal: Product-specific evidence is brand-funded only (Moyen 2024: nine of ten authors are Eight Sleep staff, fixed off-on-off order, no randomization, deep and REM gains only in sex and time-of-night subgroups), which alone would be N. The C rests on Herberger 2024 (randomized, blinded crossover, one night per mattress, +7.5 min deep sleep, about 2 bpm lower heart rate), whose co-author is affiliated with Technogel, the mattress material maker, plus a solid temperature mechanism (Okamoto-Mizuno 2012). A reviewer could fairly choose N. No independent trial of an active cooling pad was found; the Sleepme hot-flash result is a company press release. V3 said the only studies were company-run; that holds for the product. V3's 50 USD a month is too low: Pod 5 hardware runs about 2,849 to 2,999 USD plus Autopilot at 199 to 399 USD a year (third-party pricing pages, searched 2026-10-20), about 135 USD a month over 24 months. Simpler pads cost much less.

items.name: Consistent wake time (±30 min)
items.evidenceFor: feeling more alert in the day
items.evidenceSummary: Large studies link steady sleep and wake times, weekends included, to better health and longer life. A small trial in students found keeping regular times lifted daytime alertness, and sleep experts agree regularity matters.
items.humanQuestion: How far does your wake-up time drift on weekends?
items.fitsInstead: Weekend wake-ups within an hour of weekdays, rather than to the minute.
items.notesInternal: V3 graded A from one cohort; regraded B, since the brief's A needs meta-analyses or several RCTs in healthy adults. Evidence: large observational cohorts (Windred 2024: 60,977 people, mean age 63, so not the 22 to 35 group; it measured overall sleep regularity, not wake time alone), a systematic review of mostly observational studies (Chaput 2020, very low to moderate certainty), an expert consensus (Sletten 2023, National Sleep Foundation), one small controlled trial in students (Manber 1996; the abstract does not say whether groups were randomized), and stimulus control, which includes waking at the same time daily, for chronic insomnia (Edinger 2021, conditional, low-quality evidence). No trial isolates wake time alone in healthy adults. V3's '60,000 people' figure is confirmed (60,977). V3's 'single strongest sleep habit we know of' is not something these sources establish.

items.name: Screens / phone in bed
items.evidenceFor: winding down and falling asleep
items.evidenceSummary: The research finds no sleep benefit from a phone in bed. In 42 studies of young adults, heavier phone use, especially at night, went with later, shorter, worse sleep. A small trial found a phone-free half hour sped up sleep.
items.humanQuestion: What do you usually do on the phone in bed?
items.fitsInstead: Charging the phone outside the bedroom, with a book by the bed.
items.notesInternal: The tier grades the benefit people use it for (winding down), which only anecdote supports, so D; the harm evidence lives in the summary. V3 graded the harm as B, which under V4 would add EVIDENCE_REGULAR and protect the habit. Harm evidence is mostly observational (Brautsch 2023: 42 studies, causal direction unclear; Hjetland 2025: cross-sectional, 35% response rate) plus one small pilot RCT with diary-only outcomes (He 2020: 38 students, latency 31 to 18 min vs 29 to 27 min). V3's '20 to 30 minutes later for social media in bed' figure was not confirmed (Levenson 2017 and Exelmans 2016 not opened). Hjetland found no difference between social media and other screen activities, which cuts against V3's 'what you look at matters more than blue light' line; time in bed on the screen seems to matter most.

items.name: Reading (paper) before bed
items.evidenceFor: sleep that feels a little better
items.evidenceSummary: In an online trial of nearly 1,000 adults, a week of reading in bed left 42% reporting better sleep, versus 28% without. A small lab study found paper books, unlike a bright tablet, left melatonin untouched.
items.humanQuestion: Paper book, e-reader, or tablet?
items.notesInternal: V3 graded C ('small trials versus screens favour paper'); regraded B because two randomized studies agree, though both are short. Finucane 2021 is large (991 randomized) but one week long, unblinded, with a single-item self-reported outcome and more dropouts among readers; e-readers were not excluded and paper was not required. Its secondary sleep-disturbance gain was small. Chang 2015 (12 people, inpatient) compared a printed book with a tablet at full brightness for 4 hours, not with no reading. So the support is for reading in general and for print over bright screens; paper versus e-ink has not been tested. Cost set to 0 because the habit is free; books are optional.

items.name: Weekend sleep-in (over 1 h)
items.evidenceFor: making up for short sleep during the week
items.evidenceSummary: Studies disagree. In a Swedish cohort, short weekday sleepers who slept longer on weekends lived as long as steady sleepers, yet a larger device-based study found no benefit. A lab trial found catch-up shifted the body clock later.
items.humanQuestion: Is the lie-in for pleasure, or catching up on short nights?
items.fitsInstead: A lie-in kept under an hour, with an earlier night on Friday.
items.notesInternal: V3 framed it only as harmful (B, social jet lag) and left the goal blank. The evidence conflicts, so C: catch-up looked protective in a Swedish cohort (Akerstedt 2019, self-reported sleep, under-65s only) and in observational studies pooled by Chaput 2020, and the National Sleep Foundation panel endorsed catch-up when weekday sleep is short (Sletten 2023). Against that, device-measured UK Biobank data found no link with mortality or cardiovascular disease (Chaput 2024; per the Gao 2024 editorial, one sensitivity analysis hinted at higher mortality at 2 h or more), and a randomized lab study found weekend recovery delayed the body clock and did not reverse metabolic effects (Depner 2019). Taylor 2008 and Wittmann 2006 could not be opened (no abstract available), so V3's Sunday-night circadian claim rests on Depner here.

sources.citation: American Academy of Dermatology. 7 rosacea skin care tips dermatologists recommend. aad.org, last updated 2024-04-03.
sources.finding: For rosacea-prone skin, advises avoiding glycolic and lactic acids, stopping exfoliation, skipping toners, and trying a zinc oxide or titanium dioxide sunscreen if others irritate.

sources.citation: American Academy of Dermatology. How to apply sunscreen. aad.org, last updated 2025-08-15.
sources.finding: Recommends broad-spectrum, water-resistant SPF 30 or higher year-round, at least a teaspoon for the face, applied before going out and reapplied every two hours outdoors.

sources.citation: American Academy of Dermatology. What to look for: ABCDEs of melanoma. aad.org (undated page; year is the copyright year).
sources.finding: Advises seeing a board-certified dermatologist for any spot that is new, looks unlike the others, or is changing, itching or bleeding.

sources.citation: American Academy of Dermatology. 10 skin care habits that can worsen acne. aad.org (undated page; year is the copyright year).
sources.finding: Warns that scrubbing irritates skin and can flare acne, suggests giving a product 6 to 8 weeks, and recommends a dermatologist when acne persists or is deep.

sources.citation: American Academy of Dermatology. How to select anti-aging skin care products. aad.org (undated page; year is the copyright year).
sources.finding: Names sunscreen and moisturizer as the two most effective anti-aging buys, warns that starting several anti-aging products within weeks can irritate skin, and says price doesn't predict results.

sources.citation: American Academy of Dermatology. Dermatologists' top tips for relieving dry skin. aad.org, last updated 2026-01-02.
sources.finding: Recommends a fragrance-free cream or ointment, lists hyaluronic acid and glycerin among helpful ingredients, and advises a board-certified dermatologist if dryness continues.

sources.citation: American Academy of Dermatology. How to safely exfoliate at home. aad.org, last updated 2026-02-06.
sources.finding: Exfoliating alongside retinoids, retinol or benzoyl peroxide may worsen dryness or breakouts; over-exfoliating causes redness and irritation; strong methods can darken spots on darker skin.

sources.citation: American Academy of Dermatology. Is any acne treatment safe to use during pregnancy? aad.org (undated page; year is the copyright year).
sources.finding: Advises stopping tazarotene and isotretinoin in pregnancy, notes most experts stop tretinoin and adapalene, and calls short-term salicylic acid generally safe after checking with a clinician.

sources.citation: American Academy of Pediatrics Committee on Nutrition and Council on Sports Medicine and Fitness. Sports drinks and energy drinks for children and adolescents: are they appropriate? Pediatrics.
sources.finding: Pediatricians' clinical report: stimulant-containing energy drinks do not belong in the diets of children or teens.

sources.citation: Abdelhamid AS, Brown TJ, Brainard JS, et al. Omega-3 fatty acids for the primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2020;3:CD003177.
sources.finding: Across 86 RCTs, EPA+DHA made little or no difference to deaths or cardiovascular events, slightly lowered coronary events (low certainty) and cut triglycerides about 15%.
sources.population: adults with and without heart disease

sources.citation: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. Physical activity and exercise during pregnancy and the postpartum period: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 804. Obstet Gynecol 135(4):e178-e188.
sources.finding: Without obstetric or medical complications, exercise in pregnancy is safe and encouraged, and women active or vigorous before pregnancy can generally continue.

sources.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 5. Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026. Diabetes Care.
sources.finding: ADA advises consistent carbohydrate timing and amounts with fixed insulin doses, and glucose monitoring after alcohol to limit delayed lows on insulin or secretagogues.

sources.citation: Åkerstedt T, Ghilotti F, Grotta A, et al. Sleep duration and mortality – does weekend sleep matter? J Sleep Res. 2019;28(1):e12712.
sources.finding: 43,880 Swedish adults followed 13 years: under 65, short weekend sleep went with higher mortality, while short weekday sleep plus longer weekend sleep showed no added risk.

sources.citation: Akhgarjand C, Asoudeh F, Bagheri A, et al. Does Ashwagandha supplementation have a beneficial effect on the management of anxiety and stress? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Phytother Res. 2022;36(11):4115-4124.
sources.finding: Twelve trials, 1,002 adults: ashwagandha lowered anxiety and stress versus placebo, with stress benefits at 300 to 600 mg daily; certainty of evidence rated low.

sources.citation: Al-Niaimi F, Chiang NYZ. Topical vitamin C and the skin: mechanisms of action and clinical applications. J Clin Aesthet Dermatol. 2017;10(7):14-17.
sources.finding: Vitamin C generally needs more than 8% to matter and gains nothing past 20%; a pH below 3.5 aids stability, and common derivatives struggle to reach the skin.
sources.population: review of human and lab studies

sources.citation: Antonio J, Candow DG, Forbes SC, et al. Common questions and misconceptions about creatine supplementation: what does the scientific evidence really show? J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2021;18:13.
sources.finding: Without training, creatine gives at most small strength or muscle gains; 3-5 g/day saturates muscle in about four weeks; no kidney harm at recommended doses in healthy people.

sources.citation: Arab A, Rafie N, Amani R, Shirani F. The role of magnesium in sleep health: a systematic review of available literature. Biol Trace Elem Res. 2023;201(1):121-128.
sources.finding: Nine studies, 7,582 adults: observational data tied magnesium status to sleep quality, but supplement trials gave inconsistent results; larger, longer trials are needed.

sources.citation: Balban MY, Neri E, Kogon MM, et al. Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal. Cell Rep Med. 2023;4(1):100895.
sources.finding: In a one-month remote RCT of 108 adults, five daily minutes of breathwork, especially long-exhale cyclic sighing, raised positive mood more than mindfulness; anxiety fell similarly with both.

sources.citation: Baron KG, Abbott S, Jao N, Manalo N, Mullen R. Orthosomnia: are some patients taking the quantified self too far? J Clin Sleep Med. 2017;13(2):351-354.
sources.finding: Case reports describe patients seeking care for tracker-flagged short or restless sleep, trusting device data over lab tests; the paper labels this perfectionistic pursuit orthosomnia.

sources.citation: Baumel A, Muench F, Edan S, Kane JM. Objective user engagement with mental health apps: systematic search and panel-based usage analysis. J Med Internet Res. 2019;21(9):e14567.
sources.finding: Usage data from 93 popular mental health apps showed median 30-day retention near 3%; meditation apps kept about 5% of users by day 30.
sources.population: real-world users of 93 Android mental health apps

sources.citation: Bella YF, Cupido SRS, Inacio PAQ, et al. Pre-workout supplements and their effects on cardiovascular health: an integrative review. J Cardiovasc Dev Dis.
sources.finding: Across 24 studies, pre-workouts aided performance but showed conflicting cardiovascular effects, adverse or favourable, depending on dose and population; evidence was judged insufficient.
sources.population: active and inactive adults, some with heart disease history

sources.citation: Björnsson HK, Björnsson ES, Avula B, et al. Ashwagandha-induced liver injury: a case series from Iceland and the US Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network. Liver Int. 2020;40(4):825-829.
sources.finding: Five cases: jaundice-type liver injury began 2 to 12 weeks after starting ashwagandha; liver tests mostly normalized within 1 to 5 months, with no liver failure or deaths.
sources.population: five adults in Iceland and the US

sources.citation: Boghosian T, Mendez H, Boghosian N, Sayegh M, Beer J, Tosti A. Clinical applications of vitamin C in dermatology: a systematic review. J Clin Aesthet Dermatol. 2026;19(7):10-15.
sources.finding: Of 44 studies since 2020, including 20 RCTs, L-ascorbic acid was the best-validated form; many studies were small, short, open-label or industry-sponsored.
sources.population: patients and volunteers across 44 dermatology studies

sources.citation: Böhmer MN, Hamers PCM, Bindels PJE, Oppewal A, van Someren EJW, Festen DAM. Are we still in the dark? A systematic review on personal daily light exposure, sleep-wake rhythm, and mood in healthy adults from the general population. Sleep Health. 2021;7(5):610-630.
sources.finding: In 25 cross-sectional studies using wrist light sensors, everyday light exposure showed only weak or conflicting links with sleep timing, sleep quality and mood; no intervention studies qualified.
sources.population: healthy adults from the general population

sources.citation: Boyar L, White CM, Vanderlee L, et al. Exploring sociodemographic and nutrition-related correlates of meal-kit use across five countries: findings from the International Food Policy Study. Public Health Nutr.
sources.finding: Among 20,401 adults in five countries, 14% used a meal kit in the past week (18% in the US), more often younger, higher-income and health-minded people.
sources.population: adults in Canada, Australia, UK, US and Mexico

sources.citation: Brautsch LAS, Lund L, Andersen MM, Jennum PJ, Folker AP, Andersen S. Digital media use and sleep in late adolescence and young adulthood: a systematic review. Sleep Med Rev. 2023;68:101742.
sources.finding: 42 moderate-to-high-quality observational studies in 16-to-25-year-olds: more phone, computer and social media use went with shorter, poorer sleep; night-time phone use with later bedtimes and tiredness.

sources.citation: Buijze GA, Sierevelt IN, van der Heijden BCJM, Dijkgraaf MG, Frings-Dresen MHW. The effect of cold showering on health and work: a randomized controlled trial. PLoS One 11(9):e0161749.
sources.finding: Among 3,018 Dutch workers, ending showers with 30 to 90 seconds of cold cut sickness absence by 29 percent but not illness days; longer cold spells added nothing.
sources.population: healthy working adults 18 to 65 in the Netherlands

sources.citation: Bull FC, Al-Ansari SS, Biddle S, et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med 54(24):1451-1462.
sources.finding: Adults are advised 150 to 300 minutes of moderate or 75 to 150 of vigorous aerobic activity weekly, plus muscle strengthening on two or more days; any activity beats none.
sources.population: adults 18 to 64, including pregnant and postpartum women

sources.citation: Burke SM, Carron AV, Eys MA, Ntoumanis N, Estabrooks PA. Group versus individual approach? A meta-analysis of the effectiveness of interventions to promote physical activity. 2:19-35. The Birmingham repository lists the journal as J Sport Exerc Psychol but links to the BPS Sport and Exercise Psychology Review, which fits volume 2 in 2006.
sources.finding: Across 44 studies, classes built to foster group cohesion beat standard classes, while standard exercise classes did no better than home programs with some contact.

sources.citation: Cain T, Brinsley J, Bennett H, Nelson M, Maher C, Singh B. Effects of cold-water immersion on health and wellbeing: a systematic review and meta-analysis. PLoS One 20(1):e0317615.
sources.finding: Across 11 trials in healthy adults, cold immersion lowered stress only at 12 hours, did not improve mood, briefly raised inflammation; sleep and quality-of-life gains each rested on one study.

sources.citation: Carpenter JK, Andrews LA, Witcraft SM, Powers MB, Smits JAJ, Hofmann SG. Cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety and related disorders: a meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials. Depress Anxiety. 2018;35(6):502-514.
sources.finding: In 41 placebo-controlled trials (2,843 patients), CBT moderately reduced anxiety-disorder symptoms, with smaller gains for depression and quality of life.

sources.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Alcohol (Breastfeeding special circumstances: vaccines, medications and drugs).
sources.finding: Not drinking is safest while breastfeeding; up to one drink a day is not known to harm infants, ideally waiting at least 2 hours per drink before nursing.

sources.citation: Chang AM, Aeschbach D, Duffy JF, Czeisler CA. Evening use of light-emitting eReaders negatively affects sleep, circadian timing, and next-morning alertness. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2015;112(4):1232-1237.
sources.finding: Inpatient crossover, 12 young adults: reading a bright iPad for 4 hours before bed, versus a printed book, delayed sleep by 10 minutes, suppressed melatonin and shifted the clock later.

sources.citation: Chaput JP, Dutil C, Featherstone R, et al. Sleep timing, sleep consistency, and health in adults: a systematic review. Appl Physiol Nutr Metab. 2020;45(10 Suppl 2):S232-S247.
sources.finding: 41 studies, about 92,000 adults: later and more variable sleep timing and social jetlag went with worse health; weekend catch-up sleep went with better outcomes; certainty very low to moderate.

sources.citation: Chaput JP, Biswas RK, Ahmadi M, et al. Device-measured weekend catch-up sleep, mortality, and cardiovascular disease incidence in adults. Sleep. 2024;47(11):zsae135.
sources.finding: 73,513 UK adults with wrist sensors, followed 8 years: weekend catch-up sleep showed no link to mortality or cardiovascular disease, including among people sleeping under 6 weekday hours.

sources.citation: Chauvineau M, Pasquier F, Guyot V, Aloulou A, Nedelec M. Effect of the depth of cold water immersion on sleep architecture and recovery among well-trained male endurance runners. Front Sports Act Living 3:659990.
sources.finding: Ten minutes in 13 C water after an evening run did not change time to fall asleep or total sleep in 12 runners, and reduced night-time arousals.

sources.citation: Cheah KL, Norhayati MN, Yaacob LH, Abdul Rahman R. Effect of Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) extract on sleep: a systematic review and meta-analysis. PLoS One. 2021;16(9):e0257843.
sources.finding: Five trials, about 400 adults, all in India: ashwagandha extract gave a small but significant sleep benefit, larger with insomnia, 600 mg or more daily, and 8+ weeks.
sources.population: adults, healthy and with insomnia, India

sources.citation: Choi JB, Lee YG, Jeong DU. Transdermal nicotine patch effects on EEG power spectra and heart rate variability during sleep of healthy male adults. Psychiatry Investig. 2017;14(4):499-505.
sources.finding: In a double-blind crossover study of 16 young non-smoking men, a nicotine patch lengthened sleep latency and wake time and cut total sleep; overnight HRV did not differ.

sources.citation: Choi H, Cha Y, McCullough ME, Coles NA, Oishi S. A meta-analysis of the effectiveness of gratitude interventions on well-being across cultures. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2025;122(28):e2425193122.
sources.finding: A preregistered meta-analysis of 145 papers (24,804 people, 28 countries) found gratitude practices give a small rise in well-being, largest for positive mood and robust to publication bias.

sources.citation: Chung N, Bin YS, Cistulli PA, Chow CM. Does the proximity of meals to bedtime influence the sleep of young adults? A cross-sectional survey of university students. Int J Environ Res Public Health.
sources.finding: Among 793 adults aged 18 to 29, eating within 3 hours of bed was tied to more night waking, but not slower sleep onset or short sleep.

sources.citation: Cohen PA, Avula B, Wang YH, Katragunta K, Khan I. Quantity of melatonin and CBD in melatonin gummies sold in the US. JAMA. 2023;329(16):1401-1402.
sources.finding: Lab test of 25 US melatonin gummies: 22 mislabeled; melatonin ranged from 74% to 347% of label, and one product had none but contained CBD.
sources.population: 25 gummy products bought in the US in 2022

sources.citation: Convertino VA, Armstrong LE, Coyle EF, et al. American College of Sports Medicine position stand: exercise and fluid replacement. Med Sci Sports Exerc. (superseded by the 2007 stand)
sources.finding: Earlier ACSM stand: for exercise over an hour, include 0.5 to 0.7 g sodium per litre; under an hour, little difference from plain water.

sources.citation: Correia G, Magina S. Efficacy of topical vitamin C in melasma and photoaging: a systematic review. J Cosmet Dermatol. 2023;22(7):1938-1945.
sources.finding: Seven RCTs with 139 volunteers: treated skin looked smoother and objectively lighter, hydration matched placebo, and the ideal concentration remains unknown.

sources.citation: Costa LDS, Correa VAF, de Oliveira VF, et al. Risk factors for exercise-associated muscle cramps: a systematic review with meta-analysis. Muscle Nerve.
sources.finding: Across 9 longitudinal studies (11,274 people), only past cramps strongly predicted new ones; hydration and most electrolyte measures showed no consistent link.

sources.citation: Cruz-Sanabria F, Bruno S, Crippa A, et al. Optimizing the time and dose of melatonin as a sleep-promoting drug: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials and dose-response meta-analysis. J Pineal Res. 2024;76(5):e12985.
sources.finding: 26 trials in people with insomnia and healthy volunteers: effects on sleep onset and total sleep grew with dose, peaking near 4 mg; taking it earlier before bed helped.
sources.population: adults with insomnia and healthy volunteers

sources.citation: Cuijpers P, Miguel C, Harrer M, et al. Cognitive behavior therapy vs. control conditions, other psychotherapies, pharmacotherapies and combined treatment for depression: a comprehensive meta-analysis including 409 trials with 52,702 patients. World Psychiatry. 2023;22(1):105-115.
sources.finding: Across 409 trials (52,702 patients), CBT for depression had moderate-to-large effects versus usual care or waitlist, still present at 6 to 12 months.

sources.citation: Currier BS, Mcleod JC, Banfield L, et al. Resistance training prescription for muscle strength and hypertrophy in healthy adults: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis. Br J Sports Med 57(18):1211-1220.
sources.finding: Across 178 strength and 119 muscle-size trials, every lifting prescription beat no exercise; heavier loads gave the most strength, and two weekly sessions reliably built both.

sources.citation: Dautovich ND, Schreiber DR, Imel JL, et al. A systematic review of the amount and timing of light in association with objective and subjective sleep outcomes in community-dwelling adults. Sleep Health. 2019;5(1):31-48.
sources.finding: Across 45 studies of healthy adults, bright morning light went with an earlier sleep period and better self-rated sleep; bright evening light pushed sleep later and felt worse.

sources.citation: Davis DE, Choe E, Meyers J, et al. Thankful for the little things: a meta-analysis of gratitude interventions. J Couns Psychol. 2016;63(1):20-31.
sources.finding: Gratitude exercises beat neutral comparison tasks on well-being by a small margin, matched but did not beat other psychologically active exercises, and did not reduce anxiety.

sources.citation: DellaVigna S, Malmendier U. Paying not to go to the gym. Am Econ Rev 96(3):694-719.
sources.finding: Members of three US clubs on monthly plans over $70 averaged about 4.3 visits a month, paying over $17 per visit when a 10-visit pass cost $10 each.
sources.population: 7,752 members of three US health clubs

sources.citation: Demay MB, Pittas AG, Bikle DD, et al. Vitamin D for the prevention of disease: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2024;109(8):1907-1947.
sources.finding: For healthy adults 19-74, it advises against vitamin D beyond the DRI and against routine blood testing; extra vitamin D is suggested for ages 1-18, 75+, pregnancy and high-risk prediabetes.
sources.population: general population without an established indication

sources.citation: de Miranda RB, Weimer P, Rossi RC. Effects of hydrolyzed collagen supplementation on skin aging: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Int J Dermatol. 2021;60(12):1449-1461.
sources.finding: Pooling 19 RCTs (1,125 people, about 95% women), roughly 90 days of hydrolyzed collagen improved skin hydration and elasticity; the abstract does not examine trial funding.

sources.citation: Depner CM, Melanson EL, Eckel RH, et al. Ad libitum weekend recovery sleep fails to prevent metabolic dysregulation during a repeating pattern of insufficient sleep and weekend recovery sleep. Curr Biol. 2019;29(6):957-967.e4.
sources.finding: Randomized lab study of 36 young adults: weekend recovery sleep after five short nights did not stop drops in insulin sensitivity, and it delayed the body clock.

sources.citation: Ding D, Nguyen B, Nau T, et al. Daily steps and health outcomes in adults: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis. Lancet Public Health 10(8):e668-e681.
sources.finding: Versus 2,000 daily steps, 7,000 was linked to 47 percent lower risk of early death, plus less heart disease and dementia; curves bent around 5,000 to 7,000.

sources.citation: Dobiecka DP, Markiewicz-Zukowska R, Socha K, Naliwajko SK. New dietary trends: meal kit delivery services as a source of nutrients, a scoping review. Nutrients.
sources.finding: Fifteen publications on meal kits assessed nutrients by calculation only; the authors call for intervention studies to test real effects.

sources.citation: Draganich C, Erdal K. Placebo sleep affects cognitive functioning. J Exp Psychol Learn Mem Cogn. 2014;40(3):857-64.
sources.finding: Across two experiments (164 participants), being told sleep had been above or below average predicted scores on two of four cognitive tests, while self-rated sleep did not.

sources.citation: Drake C, Roehrs T, Shambroom J, Roth T. Caffeine effects on sleep taken 0, 3, or 6 hours before going to bed. J Clin Sleep Med.
sources.finding: 400 mg of caffeine at 0, 3 or 6 hours before bed cut monitor-measured sleep by over an hour; at 6 hours, self-reported loss was smaller and non-significant.

sources.citation: Ducrot P, Mejean C, Aroumougame V, et al. Meal planning is associated with food variety, diet quality and body weight status in a large sample of French adults. Int J Behav Nutr Phys Act.
sources.finding: In 40,554 French adults, planning meals ahead went with better guideline adherence, more food variety and lower odds of obesity; cross-sectional, so causality is unknown.

sources.citation: Ebrahim IO, Shapiro CM, Williams AJ, Fenwick PB. Alcohol and sleep I: effects on normal sleep. Alcohol Clin Exp Res.
sources.finding: Reviewing all known studies in healthy volunteers, alcohol at any dose sped sleep onset and steadied early sleep but disrupted the second half, and delayed REM.

sources.citation: Edinger JD, Arnedt JT, Bertisch SM, et al. Behavioral and psychological treatments for chronic insomnia disorder in adults: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline. J Clin Sleep Med. 2021;17(2):255-262.
sources.finding: AASM guideline: strong recommendation for CBT-I in chronic insomnia; conditional support for stimulus control, which includes waking at the same time daily; evidence quality low.

sources.citation: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies. Scientific Opinion on the safety of caffeine. EFSA Journal 13(5):4102 (read via EFSA's caffeine topic summary page).
sources.finding: Healthy adults: up to 400 mg daily and 200 mg at once; pregnancy: 200 mg daily. A 100 mg dose near bedtime may disturb some adults' sleep.
sources.population: healthy adults; pregnant and lactating women; children

sources.citation: Farias M, Maraldi E, Wallenkampf KC, Lucchetti G. Adverse events in meditation practices and meditation-based therapies: a systematic review. Acta Psychiatr Scand. 2020;142(5):374-393.
sources.finding: Across 83 studies (6,703 meditators), about 8% reported an adverse effect (3.7% in experimental studies), most often anxiety or depression, sometimes without earlier mental health problems.

sources.citation: US Food and Drug Administration. Alpha hydroxy acids. fda.gov, content current as of 2022-11-22.
sources.finding: After four weeks of AHA use, sensitivity to UV redness rose 18% and UV cell damage roughly doubled; the effect faded within a week of stopping.

sources.citation: US Food and Drug Administration. Spilling the Beans: How Much Caffeine Is Too Much? Consumer Update.
sources.finding: 400 mg daily is generally fine for healthy adults; energy drinks hold 54 to 328 mg per 16 oz; pregnancy, breastfeeding and some medicines merit a provider check.

sources.citation: Ferracioli-Oda E, Qawasmi A, Bloch MH. Meta-analysis: melatonin for the treatment of primary sleep disorders. PLoS One. 2013;8(5):e63773.
sources.finding: Nineteen trials, 1,683 people with primary sleep disorders: melatonin shortened time to fall asleep by about 7 minutes and added about 8 minutes of sleep; benefits held over time.
sources.population: mostly adults with primary insomnia or delayed sleep phase

sources.citation: Fincham GW, Strauss C, Montero-Marin J, Cavanagh K. Effect of breathwork on stress and mental health: a meta-analysis of randomised-controlled trials. Sci Rep. 2023;13(1):432.
sources.finding: Across 12 RCTs (785 adults), breathwork lowered self-reported stress with a small-to-medium effect and eased anxiety and depressive symptoms similarly; most trials carried moderate bias risk.
sources.population: 785 adults in 12 RCTs (nonclinical and physical-health samples)

sources.citation: Finucane E, O'Brien A, Treweek S, et al. Does reading a book in bed make a difference to sleep in comparison to not reading a book in bed? The People's Trial—an online, pragmatic, randomised trial. Trials. 2021;22:873.
sources.finding: Online pragmatic RCT, 991 adults: reading a book in bed for 15 to 30 minutes over 7 nights led 42% to report better sleep versus 28% of non-readers.
sources.population: adult volunteers recruited online from 43 countries

sources.citation: Fisher J, Steele J, Wolf M, Androulakis Korakakis P, Smith D, Giessing J. The role of supervision in resistance training; an exploratory systematic review and meta-analysis. Int J Strength Cond 2(1).
sources.finding: Across 12 studies, supervised lifting produced a small overall performance edge and a moderate, imprecise strength edge over unsupervised lifting, with almost no body-composition difference.
sources.population: adults doing resistance training, mixed training levels

sources.citation: Fleming KM, Herring MP. The effects of pilates on mental health outcomes: a meta-analysis of controlled trials. Complement Ther Med 37:80-95.
sources.finding: Eight small controlled trials found large drops in depressive symptoms, anxiety and fatigue with pilates versus no activity, but controls were inactive and study quality varied.

sources.citation: Fletcher EA, Lacey CS, Aaron M, et al. Randomized controlled trial of high-volume energy drink versus caffeine consumption on ECG and hemodynamic parameters. J Am Heart Assoc.
sources.finding: With caffeine matched at 320 mg, an energy drink raised QTc and systolic pressure more than a caffeine-only drink at some time points; heart rate did not differ.

sources.citation: Fujiwara Y, Machida A, Watanabe Y, et al. Association between dinner-to-bed time and gastro-esophageal reflux disease. Am J Gastroenterol.
sources.finding: Compared with a 4-hour or longer gap, finishing dinner under 3 hours before bed carried about 7 times the odds of reflux disease.
sources.population: 147 reflux patients and 294 matched controls in Japan

sources.citation: Gál É, Ștefan S, Cristea IA. The efficacy of mindfulness meditation apps in enhancing users' well-being and mental health related outcomes: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. J Affect Disord. 2021;279:131-142.
sources.finding: Pooling 34 RCTs (7,566 people), app-based mindfulness lowered perceived stress moderately and anxiety and depression slightly, but trials were few, varied and of uncertain bias risk.

sources.citation: Gardiner C, Weakley J, Burke LM, et al. The effect of caffeine on subsequent sleep: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sleep Med Rev.
sources.finding: Across 24 studies, caffeine cut sleep about 45 minutes and deep sleep about 11; modelled cut-offs were 8.8 h before bed for coffee, 13.2 h for pre-workout.
sources.population: healthy adults aged 18 to 65, mostly low to moderate caffeine users

sources.citation: Gardiner C, Weakley J, Burke LM, et al. The effect of alcohol on subsequent sleep in healthy adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sleep Med Rev.
sources.finding: Across 27 studies, alcohol delayed and reduced REM sleep from low doses (up to about two drinks), worsening with dose; faster sleep onset appeared only at high doses.

sources.citation: Gavriloff D, Sheaves B, Juss A, Espie CA, Miller CB, Kyle SD. Sham sleep feedback delivered via actigraphy biases daytime symptom reports in people with insomnia: implications for insomnia disorder and wearable devices. J Sleep Res. 2018;27(6):e12726.
sources.finding: In 63 adults with insomnia given fake morning sleep feedback, those told they slept poorly felt less alert and more tired by evening; measured vigilance did not differ.

sources.citation: Gencer B, Djousse L, Al-Ramady OT, et al. Effect of long-term marine omega-3 fatty acids supplementation on the risk of atrial fibrillation in randomized controlled trials of cardiovascular outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Circulation. 2021;144(25):1981-1990.
sources.finding: In seven cardiovascular trials (81,210 people), omega-3 raised atrial fibrillation risk about 25%, more in trials above 1 g/day (HR 1.49) than at 1 g or less.

sources.citation: Gonzalez AM, Townsend JR, Sapp PA, et al. Effect of AG1 supplementation on nutritional adequacy and gut microbial composition in trained adults. Front Nutr. 2026;13:1783951.
sources.finding: AG1-funded two-week crossover in 20 trained adults: more micronutrient targets met on paper, no change in microbiome diversity or digestive quality of life. Most authors AG1 employees.

sources.citation: Grgic J, Grgic I, Pickering C, et al. Wake up and smell the coffee: caffeine supplementation and exercise performance, an umbrella review of 21 published meta-analyses. Br J Sports Med.
sources.finding: Across 21 meta-analyses, caffeine improved endurance, strength, muscular endurance, power, jumping and speed, mostly with moderate-quality evidence from studies in young men.

sources.citation: Griffiths CE, Kang S, Ellis CN, et al. Two concentrations of topical tretinoin (retinoic acid) cause similar improvement of photoaging but different degrees of irritation. Arch Dermatol. 1995;131(9):1037-1044.
sources.finding: Over 48 weeks in 99 adults with photoaging, 0.025% and 0.1% tretinoin improved skin equally versus vehicle, but the stronger cream caused more redness and scaling.

sources.citation: Grimaldi D, Reid KJ, Abbott SM, Knutson KL, Zee PC. Sleep-aligned extended overnight fasting improves nighttime and daytime cardiometabolic function. Arterioscler Thromb Vasc Biol.
sources.finding: In 39 adults aged 36 to 75 with overweight, finishing eating at least 3 hours before sleep for 7.5 weeks lowered nighttime heart rate and raised HRV.
sources.population: adults aged 36 to 75 with overweight or obesity

sources.citation: Gröber U, Werner T, Vormann J, Kisters K. Myth or reality—transdermal magnesium? Nutrients. 2017;9(8):813.
sources.finding: Skin is a strong barrier to magnesium; studies of sprays, creams and baths were tiny, uncontrolled or unpublished, so transdermal magnesium lacks scientific support.
sources.population: small human studies of skin-applied magnesium

sources.citation: Gu C, Brereton N, Schweitzer A, et al. Metabolic effects of late dinner in healthy volunteers: a randomized crossover clinical trial. J Clin Endocrinol Metab.
sources.finding: In 20 healthy adults, dinner at 10pm versus 6pm left sleep stages unchanged but raised overnight glucose and cortisol and cut fat burning.

sources.citation: Guest NS, VanDusseldorp TA, Nelson MT, et al. International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: caffeine and exercise performance. J Int Soc Sports Nutr.
sources.finding: Caffeine at 3 to 6 mg/kg, usually an hour before exercise, gives small to moderate performance gains, including from caffeinated pre-workouts and energy drinks; 2 mg/kg may suffice.

sources.citation: Gulati I, Kosgoda S, Kundu A, et al. The association between e-cigarette use and sleep health: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Tob Induc Dis. 2026;24.
sources.finding: Pooling 12 cross-sectional studies, people who only vaped (no cigarettes) had about 38% higher odds of poor sleep health than never-users, in teens and adults alike.
sources.population: adolescents and adults who vape only, versus never-users

sources.citation: Haghayegh S, Khoshnevis S, Smolensky MH, Diller KR, Castriotta RJ. Before-bedtime passive body heating by warm shower or bath to improve sleep: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sleep Med Rev 46:124-135.
sources.finding: A warm bath or shower at 40 to 42.5 C taken one to two hours before bed, even for 10 minutes, shortened time to fall asleep and improved sleep quality.

sources.citation: Hannuksela ML, Ellahham S. Benefits and risks of sauna bathing. Am J Med 110(2):118-126.
sources.finding: Most healthy adults and children tolerate saunas well; unstable angina, a recent heart attack and severe aortic stenosis rule them out, and drinking in the sauna adds risk.
sources.population: healthy adults and children; people with heart disease

sources.citation: Harty PS, Zabriskie HA, Erickson JL, et al. Multi-ingredient pre-workout supplements, safety implications, and performance outcomes: a brief review. J Int Soc Sports Nutr.
sources.finding: Pre-workout blends may help muscular endurance and mood, with mixed results for strength and power; proprietary blends hide doses, and some may contain banned substances.

sources.citation: Harvey AG, Farrell C. The efficacy of a Pennebaker-like writing intervention for poor sleepers. Behav Sleep Med. 2003;1(2):115-24.
sources.finding: In a pilot of 42 poor sleepers, three nights of writing about worries and feelings shortened self-reported time to fall asleep compared with not writing.

sources.citation: Hausenblas HA, Lynch T, Hooper S, Shrestha A, Rosendale D, Gu J. Magnesium-L-threonate improves sleep quality and daytime functioning in adults with self-reported sleep problems: a randomized controlled trial. Sleep Med X. 2024;8:100121.
sources.finding: Funded by AIDP, with Magtein supplied by its maker: 1 g threonate daily (about 75 mg elemental) for 3 weeks improved ring-measured deep and REM sleep scores.
sources.population: 80 adults aged 35 to 55 with self-reported sleep problems

sources.citation: He FJ, Li J, MacGregor GA. Effect of longer term modest salt reduction on blood pressure: Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials. BMJ.
sources.finding: Across 34 trials, cutting salt by about 4.4 g a day for four weeks or more lowered blood pressure, more in people with hypertension and with larger cuts.
sources.population: adults with and without high blood pressure

sources.citation: He JW, Tu ZH, Xiao L, Su T, Tang YX. Effect of restricting bedtime mobile phone use on sleep, arousal, mood, and working memory: a randomized pilot trial. PLoS One. 2020;15(2):e0228756.
sources.finding: In a pilot RCT of 38 adults, avoiding the phone for 30 minutes before bed for four weeks shortened sleep latency, lengthened sleep and lowered pre-sleep arousal.

sources.citation: He JW, Tu ZH, Xiao L, Su T, Tang YX. Effect of restricting bedtime mobile phone use on sleep, arousal, mood, and working memory: a randomized pilot trial. PLoS One. 2020;15(2):e0228756.
sources.finding: Pilot RCT, 38 students with poor sleep: a phone-free 30 minutes before bed for 4 weeks cut diary sleep latency from 31 to 18 minutes and improved sleep quality.
sources.population: college students with poor sleep, China

sources.citation: Herberger S, Penzel T, Fietze I, et al. Enhanced conductive body heat loss during sleep increases slow-wave sleep and calms the heart. Sci Rep. 2024;14(1):4669.
sources.finding: Blinded crossover, one night per mattress, 72 adults: a cooling mattress added ~7.5 minutes deep sleep and ~2 bpm lower heart rate; one co-author is affiliated with the material maker.
sources.population: 72 adults: young men, middle-aged men and postmenopausal women

sources.citation: Herxheimer A, Petrie KJ. Melatonin for the prevention and treatment of jet lag. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2002;(2):CD001520.
sources.finding: Ten trials in travellers: melatonin markedly eased jet lag, especially flying east; 0.5 and 5 mg worked alike, 5 mg brought faster sleep, and higher doses added nothing.
sources.population: adult air travellers and airline cabin crew

sources.citation: Hjetland GJ, Skogen JC, Hysing M, Gradisar M, Sivertsen B. How and when screens are used: comparing different screen activities and sleep in Norwegian university students. Front Psychiatry. 2025;16:1548273.
sources.finding: Survey of about 45,000 Norwegian students: each extra hour of screen use after going to bed went with 59% higher odds of insomnia symptoms and 24 minutes less sleep.

sources.citation: Hoffman MD, Stuempfle KJ. Sodium supplementation and exercise-associated hyponatremia during prolonged exercise. Med Sci Sports Exerc.
sources.finding: In a 161-km race, sodium supplement intake did not separate runners with low blood sodium from others; overdrinking was the main feature.

sources.citation: Hollis-Hansen K, Haskins C, Turcios J, et al. A pilot randomized controlled trial comparing nutritious meal kits and no-prep meals to improve food security and diet quality among food pantry clients. BMC Public Health.
sources.finding: In 70 food-pantry clients, two weeks of free meal kits or ready meals both improved self-rated diet quality and food security, with no difference between them.

sources.citation: Hu Y, Hu FB, Manson JE. Marine omega-3 supplementation and cardiovascular disease: an updated meta-analysis of 13 randomized controlled trials involving 127,477 participants. J Am Heart Assoc. 2019;8(19):e013543.
sources.finding: Pooling 13 RCTs of mostly older or higher-risk adults, marine omega-3 lowered heart attacks and coronary deaths by about 8%, with no stroke effect; fish intake could not be tested.
sources.population: adults with mean age 64, many with diabetes or on statins

sources.citation: Hughes MC, Williams GM, Baker P, Green AC. Sunscreen and prevention of skin aging: a randomized trial. Ann Intern Med. 2013;158(11):781-790.
sources.finding: In 903 Australian adults under 55, daily sunscreen for about 4.5 years meant 24% less measured skin aging than using it only sometimes.

sources.citation: Hughes MC, Williams GM, Baker P, Green AC. Sunscreen and prevention of skin aging: a randomized trial. Ann Intern Med. 2013;158(11):781-790.
sources.finding: Among 903 Australian adults under 55, daily broad-spectrum sunscreen users showed no detectable rise in skin aging over 4.5 years, and 24% less aging than discretionary users.

sources.citation: Hussain J, Cohen M. Clinical effects of regular dry sauna bathing: a systematic review. Evid Based Complement Alternat Med 2018:1857413.
sources.finding: Of 40 sauna studies, only 13 were randomised and most were small; most reported benefits, and one small study found reversible drops in sperm production.

sources.citation: Iao SI, Jansen E, Shedden K, et al. Associations between bedtime eating or drinking, sleep duration and wake after sleep onset: findings from the American time use survey. Br J Nutr.
sources.finding: In US time-use data, eating or drinking within an hour of bed went with longer sleep but over twice the odds of long night waking.

sources.citation: Institute of Medicine. Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium and Vitamin D: Report Brief. National Academies, November 2010 (revised March 2011).
sources.finding: Adult RDA is 600 IU and the upper limit 4,000 IU; evidence supported bone health only; above 10,000 IU daily causes kidney and tissue damage; most North Americans meet needs.

sources.citation: Jaehne A, Loessl B, Bárkai Z, Riemann D, Hornyak M. Effects of nicotine on sleep during consumption, withdrawal and replacement therapy. Sleep Med Rev. 2009;13(5):363-77.
sources.finding: Reviewing 52 studies, nicotine use was tied to longer sleep onset, more fragmented and lighter sleep, and less REM; withdrawal also disturbs sleep for a time.
sources.population: human and animal studies of nicotine and sleep

sources.citation: Jaehne A, Unbehaun T, Feige B, Herr S, Appel A, Riemann D. The influence of 8 and 16 mg nicotine patches on sleep in healthy non-smokers. Pharmacopsychiatry. 2014;47(2):73-8.
sources.finding: In a double-blind trial of 66 healthy young non-smokers, a 16 mg nicotine patch worn overnight cut sleep time and efficiency and added wake time, dose-dependently.

sources.citation: Jäger R, Kerksick CM, Campbell BI, et al. International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: protein and exercise. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2017;14:20.
sources.finding: Most exercisers do well on 1.4-2.0 g/kg/day, with 20-40 g (about 0.25 g/kg) per serving; supplements are a convenient route; people in renal failure do better on restricted protein.

sources.citation: Jagim AR, Harty PS, Camic CL. Common ingredient profiles of multi-ingredient pre-workout supplements. Nutrients.
sources.finding: Among 100 top-selling pre-workouts, average caffeine was about 254 mg, beta-alanine sat below the effective dose, and 44% of ingredients hid in proprietary blends.

sources.citation: Jagim AR, Camic CL, Harty PS. Common habits, adverse events, and opinions regarding pre-workout supplement use among regular consumers. Nutrients.
sources.finding: Of 872 regular users (mean age 28), 89% took pre-workout for energy and focus, and 54% reported side effects such as skin reactions, heart abnormalities or nausea.

sources.citation: Jahrami H, Trabelsi K, Husain W, et al. Prevalence of orthosomnia in a general population sample: a cross-sectional study. Brain Sci. 2024;14(11):1123.
sources.finding: Among 523 adults, 36% used sleep trackers; depending on cut-offs, 3% to 14% of the sample screened positive for orthosomnia, with more severe insomnia symptoms.

sources.citation: Jolliffe DA, Camargo CA Jr, Sluyter JD, et al. Vitamin D supplementation to prevent acute respiratory infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis of aggregate data from randomised controlled trials. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2021;9(5):276-292.
sources.finding: Across 46 RCTs, a small overall drop in respiratory infections (OR 0.92), clearest with daily 400-1,000 IU; no subgroup by baseline vitamin D level showed a significant effect.

sources.citation: Jolliffe DA, Camargo CA Jr, Sluyter JD, et al. Vitamin D supplementation to prevent acute respiratory infections: systematic review and meta-analysis of stratified aggregate data. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2025;13(4):307-320.
sources.finding: With newer trials added (40 studies, 61,589 people), the effect on respiratory infections was no longer significant (OR 0.94), and baseline vitamin D status did not change it.

sources.citation: Kafi R, Kwak HS, Schumacher WE, et al. Improvement of naturally aged skin with vitamin A (retinol). Arch Dermatol. 2007;143(5):606-612.
sources.finding: In 36 older adults (mean age 87), 0.4% retinol lotion used up to three times weekly for 24 weeks reduced fine wrinkles more than vehicle.
sources.population: older adults in senior living, mean age 87

sources.citation: Kaldenbach S, Hysing M, Strand TA, Sivertsen B. Energy drink consumption and sleep parameters in college and university students: a national cross-sectional study. BMJ Open.
sources.finding: In 53,266 Norwegian students aged 18 to 35, more frequent energy drinks went with shorter, less efficient sleep and more waking; daily use roughly doubled short-sleep risk.

sources.citation: Kaplan YC, Ozsarfati J, Etwel F, Nickel C, Nulman I, Koren G. Pregnancy outcomes following first-trimester exposure to topical retinoids: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Br J Dermatol. 2015;173(5):1132-1141.
sources.finding: Among 654 pregnancies exposed to topical retinoids, major malformations and miscarriage were not clearly raised, but the authors judge the data too underpowered to justify use.
sources.population: pregnant women exposed in the first trimester

sources.citation: Kesgin YE, Hasbal NB, Copur S, et al. Effects of nighttime eating behavior on cardiometabolic health and sleep: a crossover study. Nutr Metab Cardiovasc Dis.
sources.finding: In 16 healthy adults aged 18 to 35, a week with a quarter or more of calories after 9:30pm lowered melatonin and raised cortisol and overnight breathing events.

sources.citation: Kim D, Ko EJ, Cho H, et al. Spinning-induced rhabdomyolysis: eleven case reports and review of the literature. Electrolyte Blood Press 13(2).
sources.finding: Eleven otherwise healthy women sought care with muscle breakdown two to three days after a first spinning class; all recovered, and the authors urge beginner warnings.

sources.citation: Kirby TO, Sapp PA, Townsend JR, et al. AG1 induces a favorable impact on gut microbial structure and functionality in the Simulator of Human Intestinal Microbial Ecosystem model. Curr Issues Mol Biol. 2024;46(1):557-569.
sources.finding: AG1-funded lab gut simulator using stool from three donors: AG1 shifted some bacterial groups, diversity unchanged; no human outcomes. Five authors are AG1 employees.

sources.citation: Kreider RB, Kalman DS, Antonio J, et al. International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation in exercise, sport, and medicine. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2017;14:18.
sources.finding: Monohydrate is the best-studied, effective form. Load about 0.3 g/kg/day for 5-7 days then 3-5 g/day, or use 3 g/day for 28 days (slower). Safe in healthy people.
sources.population: healthy adults and athletes, some clinical groups

sources.citation: Kritz M, Riddell H, Olsen D, Harden SM, Burke SM, Ntoumanis N, Thogersen-Ntoumani C. Individual versus group-based interventions: a systematic review and meta-analysis of physical activity, functional, psychosocial and health outcomes. Nat Hum Behav 10(6):1109-1121.
sources.finding: Across 71 studies, group formats showed small, non-significant edges over individual ones for activity and health, a clearer edge for strength and flexibility, and cohesion-building groups did better on health.
sources.population: adults in physical activity interventions (populations not detailed in the abstract)

sources.citation: Kubo T, Izawa S, Ikeda H, Tsuchiya M, Miki K, Takahashi M. Work e-mail after hours and off-job duration and their association with psychological detachment, actigraphic sleep, and saliva cortisol: a 1-month observational study for information technology employees. J Occup Health. 2021;63(1):e12300.
sources.finding: Over one month in 58 IT employees, more after-hours work email went with poorer detachment and lower actigraph sleep quality, but not with sleep duration or morning cortisol.

sources.citation: Laborde S, Allen MS, Borges U, et al. Effects of voluntary slow breathing on heart rate and heart rate variability: a systematic review and a meta-analysis. Neurosci Biobehav Rev. 2022;138:104711.
sources.finding: Pooling 223 studies, voluntary slow breathing increased vagally mediated heart rate variability during practice, right after one session, and after multi-session programs.

sources.citation: La Monica MB, Raub B, Hartshorn S, et al. The effects of AG1 supplementation on the gut microbiome of healthy adults: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2024;21(1):2409682.
sources.finding: Four weeks of AG1 in 30 healthy adults left microbiome diversity and gut symptoms unchanged versus maltodextrin; a few taxa shifted. Partly AG1-funded, two AG1 employee authors.

sources.citation: Langade D, Kanchi S, Salve J, Debnath K, Ambegaokar D. Efficacy and safety of Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) root extract in insomnia and anxiety: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study. Cureus. 2019;11(9):e5797.
sources.finding: In 58 adults with insomnia, 600 mg KSM-66 daily for 10 weeks shortened actigraphy-measured sleep onset and raised sleep efficiency versus placebo; product supplied by its maker.

sources.citation: Laukkanen T, Khan H, Zaccardi F, Laukkanen JA. Association between sauna bathing and fatal cardiovascular and all-cause mortality events. JAMA Intern Med 175(4):542-548.
sources.finding: Over about 20 years, Finnish men taking saunas 4 to 7 times weekly had far fewer sudden cardiac deaths than once-weekly users, an observational link.

sources.citation: Laukkanen JA, Laukkanen T, Kunutsor SK. Cardiovascular and other health benefits of sauna bathing: a review of the evidence. Mayo Clin Proc 93(8):1111-1121.
sources.finding: Mostly Finnish evidence links regular sauna use to lower risk of high blood pressure, heart disease and dementia; proposed reasons include better vessel function and lower blood pressure.
sources.population: mostly Finnish adults in cohort and small intervention studies

sources.citation: LeBoff MS, Chou SH, Ratliff KA, et al. Supplemental vitamin D and incident fractures in midlife and older adults. N Engl J Med. 2022;387(4):299-309.
sources.finding: Among 25,871 adults not selected for deficiency, 2,000 IU/day for about five years did not lower total, nonvertebral or hip fractures, whatever the starting level.

sources.citation: Lee YC, Lu CT, Cheng WN, Li HY. The impact of mouth-taping in mouth-breathers with mild obstructive sleep apnea: a preliminary study. Healthcare (Basel). 2022;10(9):1755.
sources.finding: Uncontrolled before-and-after study of 20 mouth-breathers with mild sleep apnea: with tape, snoring and breathing events fell about 47%, but there was no control group.
sources.population: 20 adults with mild sleep apnea who breathe through the mouth

sources.citation: Lee E, Kolunsarka I, Kostensalo J, et al. Effects of regular sauna bathing in conjunction with exercise on cardiovascular function: a multi-arm, randomized controlled trial. Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol 323(3):R289-R299.
sources.finding: In 47 inactive adults with heart risk factors, adding 15 minutes of sauna after exercise for 8 weeks lowered systolic pressure 8 mmHg more than exercise alone.
sources.population: 47 inactive adults, mean age 49, with at least one heart risk factor

sources.citation: Lin L, Chen X, Liu C, et al. Comparative efficacy of topical interventions for facial photoaging: a network meta-analysis. Sci Rep. 2025;15:26889.
sources.finding: Across 23 RCTs with 3,905 adults, retinol, tretinoin and topical isotretinoin improved fine wrinkles versus control; glycolic acid eased roughness but carried more adverse events.
sources.population: adults with facial photoaging, mostly women, mean age about 50

sources.citation: Linardon J, Messer M, Goldberg SB, Fuller-Tyszkiewicz M. The efficacy of mindfulness apps on symptoms of depression and anxiety: an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Clin Psychol Rev. 2024;107:102370.
sources.finding: Across 45 RCTs, mostly in unscreened adults, mindfulness apps produced small short-term drops in anxiety and depressive symptoms, holding up in lower-bias trials; no edge over active therapies.
sources.population: mostly unscreened adults (students, employees, general public)

sources.citation: LMNT. LMNT Recharge electrolyte drink mix, product page (brand).
sources.finding: One stick lists 1,000 mg sodium, 200 mg potassium and 60 mg magnesium, sold at $45 for 30; the brand claims 4 to 6 g sodium daily is optimal.

sources.citation: Lundekvam Berge H, Lundekvam KE, Waage S, Bjorvatn B, Pallesen S, Saxvig IW. Sleep in the age of technology: the use of sleep apps and perceived impact on sleep and sleep habits. Front Psychol. 2026;17:1726473.
sources.finding: In a survey of 1,002 Norwegian adults, 46% had used sleep apps; positive effects outweighed negative overall, but people with insomnia reported more negative effects.

sources.citation: Macdonald HM, Reid IR, Gamble GD, et al. 25-Hydroxyvitamin D threshold for the effects of vitamin D supplements on bone density: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial. J Bone Miner Res. 2018;33(8):1464-1469.
sources.finding: In 305 postmenopausal women given 400 or 1,000 IU/day for a year, bone density benefits appeared only when starting levels were at or below 30 nmol/L.

sources.citation: Machado AF, Ferreira PH, Micheletti JK, et al. Can water temperature and immersion time influence the effect of cold water immersion on muscle soreness? A systematic review and meta-analysis. Sports Med 46(4):503-514.
sources.finding: Nine randomised trials found cold water slightly better than passive rest for post-exercise soreness, with the best results around 10 to 15 C for 10 to 15 minutes.

sources.citation: Mah J, Pitre T. Oral magnesium supplementation for insomnia in older adults: a systematic review & meta-analysis. BMC Complement Med Ther. 2021;21:125.
sources.finding: Three small trials, 151 older adults with insomnia: magnesium shortened time to fall asleep by about 17 minutes; total sleep gain not significant; evidence quality low to very low.
sources.population: older adults with insomnia (mean ages about 59 to 69)

sources.citation: Mallock-Ohnesorg N, Rabenstein A, Stoll Y, et al. Small pouches, but high nicotine doses: nicotine delivery and acute effects after use of tobacco-free nicotine pouches. Front Pharmacol. 2024;15:1392027.
sources.finding: In a randomized crossover study of 15 smokers, 20 mg and 30 mg pouches raised heart rate about 12 and 25 bpm; a 6 mg pouch raised it only slightly.

sources.citation: Manber R, Bootzin RR, Acebo C, Carskadon MA. The effects of regularizing sleep-wake schedules on daytime sleepiness. Sleep. 1996;19(5):432-441.
sources.finding: College students, 4 weeks: both groups aimed for at least 7.5 hours of sleep, but those also keeping regular times reported less daytime sleepiness and better sleep efficiency.

sources.citation: Manson JE, Cook NR, Lee IM, et al. Marine n-3 fatty acids and prevention of cardiovascular disease and cancer (VITAL). N Engl J Med. 2019;380(1):23-32.
sources.finding: In 25,871 US adults over 50, 840 mg/day EPA+DHA for 5.3 years did not lower major cardiovascular events or cancer; fewer heart attacks and a low-fish-eater benefit were secondary hints.
sources.population: men 50+ and women 55+, not selected for heart risk

sources.citation: Marchant J, Khazan I, Cressman M, Steffen P. Comparing the effects of square, 4-7-8, and 6 breaths-per-minute breathing conditions on heart rate variability, CO2 levels, and mood. Appl Psychophysiol Biofeedback. 2025;50(2):261-276.
sources.finding: In 84 college students, breathing at six breaths a minute raised HRV more than box or 4-7-8 breathing; no single session meaningfully changed mood or blood pressure.

sources.citation: Martineau AR, Jolliffe DA, Hooper RL, et al. Vitamin D supplementation to prevent acute respiratory tract infections: systematic review and meta-analysis of individual participant data. BMJ. 2017;356:i6583.
sources.finding: Pooling individual data from 25 RCTs, vitamin D modestly lowered respiratory infections (OR 0.88), most in people starting very low (under 25 nmol/L) and with daily or weekly doses.
sources.population: children and adults, varied baseline levels

sources.citation: Maughan RJ, Watson P, Cordery PA, et al. A randomized trial to assess the potential of different beverages to affect hydration status: development of a beverage hydration index. Am J Clin Nutr.
sources.finding: In 72 resting men drinking 1 litre, an oral rehydration solution and milk kept more fluid than water over 4 hours; a sports drink did not.

sources.citation: Mazzetti SA, Kraemer WJ, Volek JS, et al. The influence of direct supervision of resistance training on strength performance. Med Sci Sports Exerc 32(6):1175-1184.
sources.finding: Over 12 weeks, moderately trained men coached by a personal trainer lifted heavier loads, progressed faster and ended with greater squat and bench strength than men training alone.

sources.citation: Milanovic Z, Sporis G, Weston M. Effectiveness of high-intensity interval training (HIT) and continuous endurance training for VO2max improvements: a systematic review and meta-analysis of controlled trials. Sports Med 45(10):1469-1481.
sources.finding: In 28 trials, steady endurance training raised VO2max by about 4.9 and intervals by about 5.5 mL/kg/min versus no exercise; intervals added a small extra gain.

sources.citation: Millard-Stafford M, Snow TK, Jones ML, Suh H. The beverage hydration index: influence of electrolytes, carbohydrate and protein. Nutrients.
sources.finding: In 19 young adults at rest, electrolytes alone at sports-drink levels did not reliably beat water for fluid retention; adding carbohydrate or a dipeptide did.

sources.citation: Miller DJ, Sargent C, Roach GD. A validation of six wearable devices for estimating sleep, heart rate and heart rate variability in healthy adults. Sensors (Basel). 2022;22(16):6317.
sources.finding: Worn together for one lab night by 53 adults, Oura, WHOOP, Apple Watch and three others all measured total sleep validly but classified sleep stages only fairly to moderately.

sources.citation: Momma H, Kawakami R, Honda T, Sawada SS. Muscle-strengthening activities are associated with lower risk and mortality in major non-communicable diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies. Br J Sports Med 56(13):755-763.
sources.finding: Across 16 cohort studies, muscle-strengthening was linked to 10 to 17 percent lower risk of early death, heart disease, cancer and diabetes, peaking near 30 to 60 minutes weekly.

sources.citation: Mooney P, Espie CA, Broomfield NM. An experimental assessment of a Pennebaker writing intervention in primary insomnia. Behav Sleep Med. 2009;7(2):99-105.
sources.finding: In 28 people with insomnia, three nights of Pennebaker-style worry writing eased pre-sleep arousal on one of two measures but did not shorten time to fall asleep.

sources.citation: Moore E, Fuller JT, Buckley JD, et al. Impact of cold-water immersion compared with passive recovery following a single bout of strenuous exercise on athletic performance in physically active participants: a systematic review with meta-analysis and meta-regression. Sports Med 52(7):1667-1688.
sources.finding: Across 52 studies, cold water after high-intensity exercise improved soreness, perceived recovery and power at 24 hours versus passive rest; after eccentric work only power improved.

sources.citation: Morton RW, Murphy KT, McKellar SR, et al. A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults. Br J Sports Med. 2018;52(6):376-384.
sources.finding: In 49 RCTs, protein supplements during resistance training added modest lean mass (0.3 kg) and strength (2.5 kg 1RM); gains plateaued near 1.6 g/kg/day total protein.

sources.citation: Moyen NE, Ediger TR, Taylor KM, et al. Sleeping for one week on a temperature-controlled mattress cover improves sleep and cardiovascular recovery. Bioengineering (Basel). 2024;11(4):352.
sources.finding: Company-run, unrandomized study of 54 adults: a week with the Pod's temperature control on lowered sleeping heart rate about 2%; deep and REM sleep changes appeared only in subgroups.
sources.population: 54 mostly healthy adults aged 21 to 74, sleeping at home

sources.citation: Murtagh EM, Nichols L, Mohammed MA, Holder R, Nevill AM, Murphy MH. The effect of walking on risk factors for cardiovascular disease: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised control trials. Prev Med 72:34-43.
sources.finding: In randomised trials of inactive adults, walking programs raised aerobic fitness by about 3 mL/kg/min and lowered systolic blood pressure about 3.6 mmHg, with small drops in weight and waist.

sources.citation: Myung SK, Park Y. Effects of collagen supplements on skin aging: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Am J Med. 2025;138(9):1264-1277.
sources.finding: Pooled across 23 RCTs collagen looked helpful, but trials without company funding and high-quality trials showed no effect on skin hydration, elasticity or wrinkles.

sources.citation: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NIH). Melatonin: what you need to know. Updated May 2024.
sources.finding: NIH summary: melatonin seems safe short-term, long-term safety unknown; guidelines do not back it for chronic insomnia; may ease jet lag; epilepsy or blood thinners need medical supervision.

sources.citation: NHS. Exercise in pregnancy. nhs.uk, page last reviewed 24 September 2026.
sources.finding: Advises 150 minutes of moderate activity weekly plus strength work, telling instructors about the pregnancy, keeping cool, and avoiding lying flat on the back later in pregnancy.

sources.citation: National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism. Alcohol's Effects on the Body (liver section).
sources.finding: Heavy drinking harms the liver, leading to fatty liver, inflammation, fibrosis, cirrhosis and liver cancer.

sources.citation: National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism. Harmful Interactions: Mixing Alcohol With Medicines.
sources.finding: Alcohol interacts with many common medicines, including sleep aids, pain relievers, antidepressants and allergy pills, raising risks from drowsiness to overdose; ask a pharmacist.

sources.citation: National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism. Mental Health Issues: Alcohol Use Disorder and Common Co-occurring Conditions. Core Resource on Alcohol.
sources.finding: Alcohol problems often co-occur with depression, anxiety and sleep disorders; drinking can worsen these symptoms, and some psychiatric medicines interact with alcohol.

sources.citation: National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism. Underage Drinking (fact sheet).
sources.finding: US minimum legal drinking age is 21; drinking before then can interfere with a brain still maturing into the twenties.

sources.citation: National Kidney Foundation. Sodium and Your CKD Diet: How to Spice Up Your Cooking.
sources.finding: With weaker kidneys, sodium and fluid can build up, raising blood pressure; people limiting potassium are told to avoid potassium-based salt substitutes.

sources.citation: Noetel M, Sanders T, Gallardo-Gomez D, et al. Effect of exercise for depression: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. BMJ 384:e075847.
sources.finding: In 218 trials of people with depression, walking or jogging, yoga and strength training eased symptoms most, more so at higher intensity; certainty was low to very low.
sources.population: adults meeting clinical cut-offs for depression

sources.citation: Nunes EA, Colenso-Semple L, McKellar SR, et al. Systematic review and meta-analysis of protein intake to support muscle mass and function in healthy adults. J Cachexia Sarcopenia Muscle. 2022;13(2):795-810.
sources.finding: In 74 RCTs, more daily protein slightly raised lean mass with resistance exercise (moderate certainty) but not without it (six trials, low certainty).

sources.citation: O'Connor EA, Evans CV, Ivlev I, et al. Vitamin and mineral supplements for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease and cancer: updated evidence report and systematic review for the US Preventive Services Task Force. JAMA. 2022;327(23):2334-2347.
sources.finding: Across 84 studies, supplements gave little or no protection against heart disease, cancer or death; multivitamins showed a small drop in cancer incidence (OR 0.93) with limitations.

sources.citation: Okamoto-Mizuno K, Mizuno K. Effects of thermal environment on sleep and circadian rhythm. J Physiol Anthropol. 2012;31:14.
sources.finding: Heat and humidity during sleep raise wakefulness and cut deep and REM sleep, mostly early in the night; falling core temperature goes with falling asleep.

sources.citation: Okereke OI, Reynolds CF, Mischoulon D, et al. Effect of long-term vitamin D3 supplementation vs placebo on risk of depression or clinically relevant depressive symptoms and on change in mood scores: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2020;324(5):471-480.
sources.finding: In 18,353 adults aged 50+, 2,000 IU/day for 5.3 years did not lower depression risk or change mood scores compared with placebo.
sources.population: adults 50+ without depression at the start

sources.citation: Paluch AE, Bajpai S, Bassett DR, et al. Daily steps and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis of 15 international cohorts. Lancet Public Health 7(3):e219-e228.
sources.finding: Among 47,471 adults, more steps meant lower death risk, levelling at about 6,000 to 8,000 daily steps after 60 and 8,000 to 10,000 before 60.

sources.citation: Pascoe MC, Bauer IE. A systematic review of randomised control trials on the effects of yoga on stress measures and mood. J Psychiatr Res 68:270-282.
sources.finding: Across 25 randomised trials, yoga was linked to fewer depressive and anxious symptoms and better stress-system regulation; the authors call the evidence preliminary.

sources.citation: Pascoe MC, Thompson DR, Ski CF. Yoga, mindfulness-based stress reduction and stress-related physiological measures: a meta-analysis. Psychoneuroendocrinology 86:152-168.
sources.finding: In 42 randomised trials against active controls, yoga postures lowered evening and waking cortisol, ambulatory systolic pressure, resting heart rate, fasting glucose and cholesterol; interventions varied widely.

sources.citation: Pavicic T, Gauglitz GG, Lersch P, et al. Efficacy of cream-based novel formulations of hyaluronic acid of different molecular weights in anti-wrinkle treatment. J Drugs Dermatol. 2011;10(9):990-1000.
sources.finding: In 76 women aged 30 to 60, 0.1% hyaluronic acid creams used twice daily for 60 days raised hydration and elasticity versus vehicle; co-authors worked for ingredient makers.
sources.population: women aged 30 to 60 with wrinkles around the eyes

sources.citation: Philips CA, Valsan A, Theruvath AH, et al. Ashwagandha-induced liver injury: a case series from India and literature review. Hepatol Commun. 2023;7(10):e0270.
sources.finding: Indian case series: ashwagandha was linked to mostly cholestatic liver injury; three people with existing chronic liver disease developed liver failure and died.
sources.population: patients with liver injury after single-ingredient ashwagandha products, India

sources.citation: Pietila J, Helander E, Korhonen I, et al. Acute effect of alcohol intake on cardiovascular autonomic regulation during the first hours of sleep in a large real-world sample of Finnish employees: observational study. JMIR Ment Health.
sources.finding: Within 4,098 adults' own nights, alcohol raised early-sleep heart rate (1.4, 4.0, 8.7 bpm at low, moderate, high intake) and lowered HRV, dose by dose.

sources.citation: Pinero A, Burke R, Augustin F, et al. Throwing cold water on muscle growth: a systematic review with meta-analysis of the effects of postexercise cold water immersion on resistance training-induced hypertrophy. Eur J Sport Sci 24(2):177-189.
sources.finding: Pooling eight studies, cold water within about 15 minutes after lifting modestly reduced muscle growth compared with lifting alone; evidence quality was fair to poor.
sources.population: mostly young adult men who lift

sources.citation: Pinnell SR, Yang H, Omar M, et al. Topical L-ascorbic acid: percutaneous absorption studies. Dermatol Surg. 2001;27(2):137-142.
sources.finding: In pig skin, L-ascorbic acid absorbed only below pH 3.5 and peaked at 20%; magnesium ascorbyl phosphate, ascorbyl palmitate and dehydroascorbic acid did not raise skin levels.

sources.citation: Proksch E, Segger D, Degwert J, et al. Oral supplementation of specific collagen peptides has beneficial effects on human skin physiology: a double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Skin Pharmacol Physiol. 2014;27(1):47-55.
sources.finding: In 69 women aged 35-55, 2.5 or 5 g/day of collagen peptides for eight weeks improved skin elasticity versus placebo; moisture changes were not significant.

sources.citation: Rawji A, Peltier MR, Mourtzanakis K, et al. Examining the effects of supplemental magnesium on self-reported anxiety and sleep quality: a systematic review. Cureus. 2024;16(4):e59317.
sources.finding: Fifteen small, mixed trials: five of eight sleep studies reported benefit; the two negative ones used the lowest doses; authors suspect low-magnesium people respond best.
sources.population: varied groups, including older adults with poor sleep, PCOS, post-surgery and restless legs

sources.citation: Reimers AK, Knapp G, Reimers CD. Effects of exercise on the resting heart rate: a systematic review and meta-analysis of interventional studies. J Clin Med 7(12):503.
sources.finding: Pooling 191 controlled studies, every type of exercise lowered resting heart rate, with endurance training and yoga the only types reducing it significantly in both men and women.

sources.citation: Rhee J, Iansavitchene A, Mannala S, Graham ME, Rotenberg B. Breaking social media fads and uncovering the safety and efficacy of mouth taping in patients with mouth breathing, sleep disordered breathing, or obstructive sleep apnea: a systematic review. PLoS One. 2025;20(5):e0323643.
